PROJECT NO. 59142

ELECTRIC RELIABILITY COUNCIL OF TEXAS, INC.’S 
REQUESTS FOR GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTIONS RELATING TO 
BATCH ZERO DEADLINES AND STATUS UPDATE ON 
ADDITIONAL MATTERS INCLUDING THE LONG-TERM LOAD FORECAST

On August 3, 2026, Governor Greg Abbott issued a letter directing the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) and Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) to conduct “a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT’s interconnection process.”  The Governor further directed that this verification and audit be completed before any additional data centers are approved to move forward.  The Commission and ERCOT interpret data centers as including virtual currency mining facilities and other computational loads.  In response, ERCOT is temporarily pausing its transitional large load interconnection study process, known as Batch Zero, until the verification and audit are complete.  During the pause, ERCOT will verify the accuracy of information large load developers submitted in support of their interconnection requests.  As part of the same effort, ERCOT will request the community impact information identified in the Governor’s letter from all data centers and virtual currency mining facilities of 25 MW or more that have not yet energized.  The verification and audit will take several months, so ERCOT was unable to meet an initial classification deadline in its rules for the Batch Zero study process.  That delay will affect subsequent steps in the Batch Zero process, including quarterly stability assessments (QSA).  ERCOT also requires additional time to review and notify developers of dynamic model deficiencies.  ERCOT therefore requests good cause exceptions under 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.3(b) authorizing ERCOT to deviate from the requirements in ERCOT Planning Guide §§ 5 and 9 governing QSAs and Batch Zero deadlines.  Due to the delay in classification of large loads for Batch Zero, ERCOT also provides an update on the impacts of the delay on the Long-Term Load Forecast (LTLF) and other processes.  
For the convenience of the Commission, a Draft Proposed Order that would grant the requested relief is provided as Attachment A. 
Background
The Batch Zero Process
On June 18, 2026, the Commission approved ERCOT Planning Guide Revision Request 145, Batch Zero Process for Large Load Interconnections (PGRR 145), and Nodal Protocol Revision Request 1325, Related to PGRR 145, Batch Zero Process for Large Load Interconnections.  PGRR 145 establishes Batch Zero, a one-time transitional interconnection study process, the Batch Zero Interconnection Study, for ERCOT to evaluate, on a system-wide basis, the reliability impacts of interconnection requests for loads that are 75 MW or more (Large Loads) that meet study maturity and commitment criteria.  
PGRR 145 categorizes Large Loads into three groups: load that has already been sufficiently studied for interconnection and therefore is considered “base load” for the Batch Zero Interconnection Study; load that requires additional study in Batch Zero—“studied load;” and load that has not met sufficient criteria to be included in Batch Zero and therefore will require study in a future interconnection process.  An Interconnecting Large Load Entity (ILLE) seeking to include a Large Load in Batch Zero as base load must qualify under one of seven eligibility paths; studied load has one path.  Several of the eligibility paths require the ILLE to satisfy commercial readiness criteria such as having site control; ordering all equipment that has a lead time of at least 18 months, with delivery sufficiently in advance of the requested Initial Energization date; obtaining all discretionary approvals required by the applicable municipality or governmental entity; and posting financial security for system upgrades.  The ILLE must submit an attestation of its compliance with the commercial readiness criteria to its Interconnecting Distribution Service Provider (DSP) or Transmission Service Provider (TSP).  The Interconnecting DSP or TSP must in turn inform ERCOT, by July 24, 2026, that the ILLE attested that it satisfied the criteria.
Planning Guide § 9.3.1 sets out the timeline for Batch Zero.  ERCOT must classify each Large Load into one of the three categories and communicate the classification to the Interconnecting DSP or TSP by August 7, 2026.  On the same day, ERCOT must notify ILLEs of any deficiencies in their dynamic data.  ILLEs have until August 31, 2026 to cure any deficiencies with their dynamic data or be removed from Batch Zero.  ERCOT must communicate the results of the Batch Zero Interconnection Study to Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs on or before April 9, 2027.  ERCOT planned to begin the study in September 2026 to meet that deadline.
Paragraph (8) of Planning Guide § 9.1 permits ERCOT to request supporting materials for any attestation provided by an ILLE, and to perform site-readiness verification through April 9, 2027.  Because only two weeks separated the July 24 attestation notice from the August 7 classification deadline, ERCOT planned to conduct verification after the Batch Zero Interconnection Study began.  Because the Governor’s directive requires this verification before classification in Batch Zero, rather than during the study period as § 9.1(8) contemplates, ERCOT did not complete classification by the August 7 deadline.
The Governor’s directive and ERCOT’s response
Governor Abbott’s August 3, 2026 letter directs the Commission and ERCOT to “conduct a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT’s interconnection process before any additional data centers are approved to move forward.”  The letter also identifies several categories of community impact information that data centers must provide to the Commission and ERCOT concerning each data center’s financial self-sufficiency, power supply, water use and cooling technology, community-impact mitigation, and ownership and controlling interests.  In response to the letter, ERCOT delayed classification of all Large Loads in Batch Zero until ERCOT completes the verification.  ERCOT will also refrain from granting further approvals to energize any Large Load data centers or virtual currency mining facilities until the verification has been completed.  ERCOT issued a Market Notice informing stakeholders that it will not meet the August 7, 2026 deadline in Planning Guide § 9.3.1 to notify each Interconnecting DSP and TSP of any Large Load’s classification.  ERCOT further committed to file, in advance of the Commission’s August 20, 2026 Open Meeting, a request for a good cause exception related to the timelines and processes for Batch Zero. 
Requests for Good Cause Exceptions
Due to the length of time necessary to conduct the verification process, ERCOT requests authorization to deviate from the Batch Zero timelines and processes in Planning Guide §§ 5 and 9.  ERCOT is working on the scope and timing of the verification process and will submit a subsequent filing for the August 20, 2026 Open Meeting to provide additional details.  ERCOT also requests authorization to include in the August 1, 2026 and November 1, 2026 QSAs those Large Loads that Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs requested classification as base load in Batch Zero with an Initial Energization date in the first or second quarter of 2027, even though ERCOT will not classify them until a later date.  These loads must meet all other QSA inclusion criteria.  Finally, ERCOT requests authorization to notify ILLEs of deficiencies in their dynamic data submissions after the August 7, 2026 deadline.
If the Commission approves these requests to deviate from the Batch Zero timelines and processes, ERCOT will issue a Market Notice to inform stakeholders.
Request to deviate from the Batch Zero classification and study deadlines
Pursuant to 16 TAC § 25.3(b), ERCOT requests that the Commission grant ERCOT an exception to 16 TAC § 25.361(b)(16) for good cause.  That rule requires ERCOT to perform its duties under ERCOT rules, which include the ERCOT Planning Guide.  ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.3.1(2)(a) requires as follows:
(a)	Interconnecting Distribution Service Providers (DSPs) and Interconnecting Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) must provide to ERCOT all information required by Sections 9.2.1.1, Eligibility Criteria for Inclusion of a Large Load as Base Load not Subject to Additional Study in the Batch Zero Process, 9.2.1.2, Eligibility Criteria for Inclusion as Load to be Studied and Allocated in Batch Zero, and 9.2.2, Submission of Large Load Information for Batch Zero Process, on or before July 24, 2026. ERCOT will notify each Interconnecting DSP and Interconnecting TSP of how each Large Load submitted under Section 9.2.2 is included and classified in the Batch Zero Interconnection Study according to the methodology defined in Section 9.2.1, Applicability of the Batch Zero Process, on or before August 7, 2026.
Good cause exists to deviate from the August 7, 2026 classification deadline in Planning Guide § 9.3.1(2)(a) because ERCOT could not both meet that deadline and complete the verification process described in Governor Abbott’s August 3, 2026 letter.  ERCOT is currently developing a comprehensive process to verify that all Large Loads included in Batch Zero satisfy applicable Planning Guide Section 9.2.1 eligibility criteria and to collect additional information from developers of data centers and virtual currency mining facilities, including the community impact information described in the Governor’s letter.  The process is expected to take several months and is described in more detail in Section III.B. below.
Request to include Large Loads in QSAs before they are classified as base load
Pursuant to 16 TAC § 25.3(b), ERCOT requests that the Commission grant ERCOT an exception to 16 TAC § 25.361(b)(16) for good cause.  That rule requires ERCOT to perform its duties under ERCOT rules, which include the ERCOT Planning Guide.  ERCOT Planning Guide § 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii) requires a Large Load to meet the requirements of Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1) to be included in a QSA that has a prerequisite deadline of August 1, 2026, November 1, 2026, February 1, 2027, or May 1, 2027.  ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1) provides that a Large Load will be classified as “base load” if it qualifies for that designation under any one of the seven eligibility paths.  Because ERCOT now intends to delay its classification of Large Loads for several months to complete the verification process required by the Governor’s letter, no Large Load will be able to meet the QSA qualification requirement under Planning Guide § 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii) during this period.        
Good cause exists to deviate from ERCOT Planning Guide § 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii) so that ERCOT can include in the August 1, 2026 and November 1, 2026 QSAs those Large Loads that Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs requested be classified as base load and that ERCOT determined are eligible to qualify as base load but has not yet formally classified.  Six Large Loads are expected to be in the August 1 QSA based on projected energization dates in January through March 2027.  Seventeen Large Loads are potentially eligible for the November 1 QSA based on projected energization dates in April through June 2027.  Absent a good cause exception, these Large Loads would be excluded from the August 1 and November 1 QSAs and would therefore be ineligible to energize on their projected energization dates solely because ERCOT has not completed the verification-dependent classification.  QSA inclusion does not by itself authorize energization.  ERCOT will allow a Large Load included in the August 1 or November 1 QSA to energize only once ERCOT’s verification process confirms that the Large Load has met the requirements to be classified as base load and the Large Load meets all other conditions for energization.  But preserving these loads’ place in the August 1 and November 1 QSAs ensures they will not be subject to unnecessary delay once the verification period has concluded, assuming the verification confirms each of these loads is eligible for base load classification.  ERCOT therefore requests authorization to include these Large Loads in the August 1, 2026 and November 1, 2026 QSAs before classification is complete.  If ERCOT determines through the verification process that a Large Load does not qualify as base load, the Large Load will not be authorized for energization until it participates in a future QSA.  Including Large Loads not yet classified as base load in the current QSA will not impair ERCOT’s ability to complete the QSA consistent with the deadline defined in ERCOT Planning Guide Section 5.3.5(2).  ERCOT will ensure that actual constraints imposed in real time do not include any Large Load that is classified as non-base load.
Batch Zero dynamic model review and deficiency notifications
  Pursuant to 16 TAC § 25.3(b), ERCOT requests that the Commission grant ERCOT an exception to 16 TAC § 25.361(b)(16) for good cause.  That rule requires ERCOT to perform its duties under ERCOT rules, which include the ERCOT Planning Guide.  ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.2(3)(a) requires ERCOT to notify an ILLE of any deficiencies in its dynamic data no later than August 7, 2026.  ILLEs must resolve any deficiencies no later than August 31, 2026, or they will be removed from Batch Zero.
ERCOT received over 200 dynamic data submissions.  It has reviewed the majority and notified the relevant ILLE of any deficiencies.  Due to internal processing constraints and variation in how ILLEs submitted their data, however, ERCOT has been unable to review all the dynamic data submissions by August 7, 2026.  ERCOT will complete its review of the remaining dynamic data submissions and notify ILLEs of any deficiencies as soon as possible.  For any ILLE notified after August 7, 2026, ERCOT requests that the ILLE be permitted to cure the deficiency within 24 days of notification, the same cure period provided under § 9.2.2(3)(a).
Additional Matters
ERCOT raises the following additional matters for the Commission’s awareness.  ERCOT does not request a ruling or exception on these matters in this filing.
Batch Zero deadlines for which ERCOT is not requesting relief
While ERCOT must delay the start of the Batch Zero Interconnection Study, it is not at this time requesting authorization to move the April 9, 2027 deadline to provide the Batch Zero Interconnection Study results to all Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs.  ERCOT does not yet know how long the verification and audit process will take or how the delay will impact the study timeline.  If necessary, ERCOT will address that deadline with another good cause exception request or through the stakeholder process.  
Verification and audit process
ERCOT expects to begin the verification and audit process shortly after the August 20, 2026 Open Meeting.  ERCOT and Commission Staff will coordinate on the process design to ensure the directives in Governor Abbott’s August 3, 2026 letter are met.  The process will take several months.  ERCOT, with support from its outside counsel and any other third parties, will issue requests for information (RFIs) to all ILLEs with Large Loads submitted for inclusion in Batch Zero.  The RFIs will be sent to ILLEs through their Interconnecting DSP or TSP.  ERCOT will use the responses to verify each ILLE’s eligibility attestation, confirming that each attesting ILLE satisfied the commercial readiness criteria on which its classification depends.  If ERCOT finds that an ILLE submitted an attestation that is false in any material respect, or that an ILLE failed to respond to the RFI, ERCOT will classify the associated Large Load as ineligible for Batch Zero.  Separately, ERCOT will use RFIs to collect additional information from developers of data centers and virtual currency mining facilities, including the community impact information described in the Governor’s letter.  A failure to respond to these questions will be reflected in the report, in a manner that protects confidential information.
ERCOT will also collect the community impact information identified in the Governor’s letter from all data centers and virtual currency mining facilities greater than 25 MW and less than 75 MW that have not yet energized.  Based on an earlier RFI related to the 2026 Regional Transmission Plan, ERCOT is aware of 258 medium-sized loads (loads with a peak demand of at least 25 MW but less than 75 MW) seeking interconnection to the ERCOT system by 2032, representing 13,473 MW.  Of those interconnection requests, approximately 157 are data centers or virtual currency mining facilities, representing 8,766 MW.  ERCOT will collaborate with DSPs and TSPs to update the medium-sized loads and collect the information from these data centers and virtual currency mining facilities. 
ERCOT will conduct this verification and audit process transparently.  It will handle information obtained, and report the results, in a manner that protects customer information consistent with ERCOT Protocols § 1.3.1.1(1)(r), Planning Guide § 9.1(3), and applicable Commission rules.  ERCOT will work with Commission Staff throughout the verification and audit process and will provide the Commission with periodic updates.  At the conclusion of the process, ERCOT will compile the results of the verification and the community impact information collected into a report and file it with the Commission.  
Effect of the classification delay on the LTLF and related assessments
ERCOT develops an LTLF each year for use in transmission planning studies and resource adequacy assessments.  ERCOT initially developed the LTLF for 2026 using criteria from the 2026 RTP Compliance Plan, which established interim criteria for the inclusion of the load of a Large Load customer in ERCOT’s load forecasts until the permanent criteria recently adopted in 16 TAC § 25.370 can be implemented.  After reviewing the forecast—278,003 MW peak load in 2029 and 367,790 MW peak load in 2032—ERCOT informed the Commission that it had concerns with using these values in the 2026 Triennial Reliability Assessment (Reliability Assessment) and in its transmission and resource adequacy analyses.  In May of this year, ERCOT requested to adjust the forecasted demand from Large Load in the 2026 LTLF using either a historical realization rate or the level of base load from the Large Load Batch Zero process.  On June 18, 2026, the Commission approved ERCOT’s request to adjust the 2026 LTLF to incorporate the Large Loads classified as base load in Batch Zero.
Until the Governor’s August 3, 2026 letter, ERCOT expected to finalize the LTLF using the Batch Zero base load information by mid-August 2026.  An extension of time to classify Large Loads in Batch Zero will further delay a final LTLF, which in turn will delay the Reliability Assessment and could delay the December 2026 Capacity, Demand, and Reserves Report.  However, even with the additional delay, incorporating verified Batch Zero base loads into the LTLF will produce a more accurate and realistic forecast than alternative methodologies, which justifies this delay.  Therefore, ERCOT is not seeking an adjustment to the LTLF methodology in this filing.  
Future, limited good cause exception filing related to the Batch Zero eligibility criteria
PGRR 145 was adopted and implemented on a compressed timeline. As a result, not all ILLEs were able to demonstrate strict compliance with all applicable eligibility criteria.  On July 23, 2026, ERCOT issued a Market Notice allowing an ILLE in that position to explain why it warrants a good cause exception from the applicable criterion.  ERCOT received 41 such requests, each seeking an exception in whole or in part from one or more Batch Zero eligibility requirements.  Although the Market Notice expressly states that the requirement to have a qualifying interconnection study is not subject to the good cause exception process, 21 of the requests seek an exception related to that study requirement.  Some ILLEs requested that ERCOT complete the review of submitted studies under the interconnection process that ended on July 10, when PGRR145 became effective.  That study review process is closed.  ERCOT will not resume those reviews and will not submit the 21 requests to the Commission as part of a good cause exception filing.  Therefore, these ILLEs will be ineligible to have their Large Load included in Batch Zero unless they are separately eligible for classification as studied load.  ERCOT will also not consider exceptions from the July 10, 2026 deadline for an ILLE to submit dynamic models for its Large Load.  The remaining good cause requests will be part of the verification and audit process; however, an ILLE requesting a good cause exception should not infer any outcome regarding that request by virtue of being part of the verification and audit process.  These other requests seek an exception from financial security requirements, the Form W submission deadline, or some combination of these.  ERCOT is evaluating each request and determining whether to seek an exception from the Commission.  That process is distinct from the good cause exception ERCOT requests in this filing, and ERCOT will address any ILLE requests warranting an exception in a future, separate filing.
Conclusion
ERCOT appreciates the Commission’s consideration of these requests for good cause exception to deviate from the Batch Zero timelines and processes.  In summary, ERCOT highlights the following key takeaways:
The Batch Zero Interconnection Study is temporarily paused until the Commission and ERCOT complete the verification and audit process of information submitted by data centers, including virtual currency mining facilities, as directed by the Governor’s August 3, 2026 letter.
ERCOT will not approve any authorizations to energize data center Large Loads until the verification and audit process is complete and such Large Loads have met the Batch Zero verification requirements.
Consistent with the Governor’s letter, ERCOT will seek community impact information from all data centers and virtual currency mining facilities with at least 25 MW of expected demand.  These information requests will be sent to applicable Interconnecting Distribution Service Providers and Transmission Service Providers.
To move forward with the verification and audit process, ERCOT requests a good cause exception from the August 7, 2026 classification deadline in Batch Zero.  Further, ERCOT requests a good cause exception from the August 1 and November 1, 2026 quarterly stability assessments to allow eligible Large Loads into those assessments to avoid unnecessary delay.
Lastly, ERCOT requests a good cause exception to continue to review dynamic data submissions after the August 7, 2026 deadline and allow ILLEs the same 24-day period to cure any identified deficiencies as contemplated in the Planning Guide.
ERCOT recommends delaying the publication of the Long-Term Load Forecast until a final base load Batch Zero classification is determined.  This delay in turn will delay the Reliability Assessment results, which were expected in November 2026. 
The verification and audit process will take several months and more details on the scope and timing will be provided at the August 20, 2026 Open Meeting.  
ERCOT would be pleased to provide any additional information the Commission may need in considering these requests.  ERCOT personnel will be available for questions at the Commission’s Open Meetings on August 14, 2026 and August 20, 2026.

PROJECT NO. 59142


DRAFT PROPOSED ORDER GRANTING GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTIONS

On August 3, 2026, Governor Greg Abbott issued a letter directing the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) and Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) to conduct “a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT’s interconnection process.”  The Governor further directed that this verification and audit be completed before any additional data centers are approved to move forward.  In response, ERCOT intends to temporarily pause its transitional Batch Zero interconnection study of loads that are 75 MW or more (Large Loads), including data centers and virtual currency mining facilities, until the verification and audit are complete.  
On August 10, 2026, ERCOT filed with the Commission a request for good cause exceptions, pursuant to 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.3(b), to the requirement of 16 TAC § 25.361(b)(16), to allow ERCOT to deviate from ERCOT Planning Guide §§ 9.2.2(3)(a), 9.3.1(2)(a), and 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii).  ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.3.1(2)(a) requires ERCOT to classify Large Loads as base load, studied load, or load that has not met sufficient criteria to be included in Batch Zero by August 7, 2026.  During the pause of the Batch Zero study, ERCOT will verify the accuracy of information Large Load developers submitted in support of their interconnection requests.  As part of the same effort, ERCOT will request the community impact information identified in the Governor’s letter from all data centers and virtual currency mining facilities of 25 MW or more that have not yet energized.  The verification and audit will take several months, so ERCOT was unable to meet an initial classification deadline in its rules for the Batch Zero study process.  
Given the delay in classifying Large Loads, ERCOT further requests an exception from the requirement in ERCOT Planning Guide § 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii) that ERCOT include in the August 1 and November 1, 2026 quarterly stability assessments (QSAs) only those Large Loads it has classified as base load.  ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1) provides that a Large Load will be classified as base load if it qualifies for that designation under any one of the seven eligibility paths.  Because ERCOT now intends to delay its classification of Large Loads for several months to complete the verification process required by the Governor’s letter, no Large Load will be able to meet the QSA qualification requirement in Planning Guide § 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii) during this period.  To avoid unnecessary delay, ERCOT requests to allow those Large Loads that Interconnecting Distribution Service Providers (DSPs) and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) submitted as base load and that ERCOT has determined are eligible to qualify as base load but has not yet classified to be included in the August 2026 and November 2026 QSAs.
ERCOT also requests authorization to allow it to continue to review dynamic data submissions after the August 7, 2026 deadline in ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.2(3)(a).  ERCOT was unable to review all the dynamic data submissions by the deadline due to internal processing constraints and variations in how Interconnecting Large Load Entities (ILLEs) submitted their data.  ERCOT intends to complete its review of the remaining dynamic data submissions and notify ILLEs of any deficiencies as soon as possible.  ERCOT further requests ILLEs be permitted to cure any deficiencies within 24 days of notification, which is the same cure period provided under § 9.2.2(3)(a). 
Good cause exists to allow ERCOT to complete the verification and audit and report the results to the Commission before continuing the Batch Zero interconnection process.  In accordance with 16 TAC § 25.3(b), the Commission grants ERCOT a good cause exception from the requirements of 16 TAC § 25.361(b)(16) that ERCOT (1) classify Large Loads by the August 7, 2026 deadline in accordance with ERCOT Planning Guide §§ 9.3.1(2)(a); and (2) include in the August 1 and November 1, 2026 QSAs only those Large Loads that ERCOT has classified as base load under ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1).  The exceptions permit ERCOT to delay classifying Large Loads for inclusion in Batch Zero and include in those QSAs Large Loads that Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs submitted as base load and that ERCOT has determined are eligible to qualify as base load but has not yet classified.  Good cause also exists to allow ERCOT to review dynamic data submissions after the August 7, 2026 deadline in ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.2(3)(a) and allow ILLEs to cure deficiencies within 24 days of notification.

        B.      Verification and audit process

        ERCOT expects to begin the verification and audit process shortly after the August 20,
2026 Open Meeting. ERCOT and Commission Staff will coordinate on the process design to
ensure the directives in Governor Abbott's August 3,2026 letter are met. The process will take
several months. ERCOT, with support from its outside counsel and any other third parties, will
issue requests for information (RFIs) to all ILLEs with Large Loads submitted for inclusion in
Batch Zero. The RFIs will be sent to ILLEs through their Interconnecting DSP or TSP. ERCOT
will use the responses to verify each ILLE' s eligibility attestation, confirming that each attesting
ILLE satisfied the commercial readiness criteria on which its classification depends. If ERCOT
finds that an ILLE submitted an attestation that is false in any material respect, or that an ILLE
failed to respond to the RFI, ERCOT will classify the associated Large Load as ineligible for Batch
Zero. Separately, ERCOT will use RFIs to collect additional information from developers of data
centers and virtual currency mining facilities, including the community impact information
